Row 4: Operational Execution Wins vs Headwinds & Call Q&A Forensic Audit

What Management Did Right (Operational Wins)

  • Explosive Cloud Inference Growth: GAAP cloud and services revenue surged +265% YoY to $141.93M as customer token demand across OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol and enterprise customers spiked.
  • 700 MW Contracted Power Footprint: Added 100 MW of energized data center capacity in Q3, securing high-density power across North America and Europe to support gigawatt-scale pipeline.
  • Commercial Expansion Beyond G42: Closed definitive commercial agreements with two new hyperscalers and confirmed Oracle Cloud Infrastructure deployment starting in 2027.
  • Blockbuster Q4 & FY2026 Guidance Raise: Raised Q4 Core revenue guide to $310M-$330M (vs $267.5M consensus) with Core gross margin expanding to 47%-49% and operating margin reaching breakeven (-1% to +1%).

Execution Challenges & Headwinds (Operational Drags)

  • GAAP Revenue Optical Miss: Consolidated GAAP revenue of $210.81M missed consensus ($214.70M) by -$3.89M due to non-cash warrant amortization charges.
  • Heavy Capital Expenditure Intensity: CapEx reached $497.19M in Q3 ($1,046.06M YTD), widening quarterly True Free Cash burn to -$871.45M.
  • Near-Term GAAP Operating Losses: GAAP operating loss widened to -$224.15M as CS-4 tape-out engineering and next-generation software development scaled ahead of revenue recognition.
  • Customer Concentration Dynamics: While two new hyperscalers signed on, the timing of multi-megawatt cluster acceptance remains subject to customer datacenter energization schedules.
Earnings Call Q&A Forensic Highlights (Hardest Analyst Questions)
Toshiya Hari (Goldman Sachs) — Wafer Supply Bottlenecks & TSMC Advanced Node Transitions

Question: Andrew, with data center commitments jumping to 700 MW and Q4 revenue guided up to $320M, are you facing any allocation limits at TSMC for monolithic 5nm wafers, and when will Cerebras transition to 3nm/2nm for the next-generation CS-4/CS-5 accelerators?

Executive Answer: Andrew Feldman (CEO): 'We have secured 100% of the TSMC wafer supply required to meet both our Q4 guide and our plan to triple revenue in 2027. Because we use monolithic wafer-scale silicon rather than advanced CoWoS packaging or HBM memory stacks, we completely bypass the industry's biggest supply chain choke points. CS-4 tape-out is on schedule, and we see zero silicon gating for our delivery roadmap.'

Forensic Assessment: STRONG REASSURANCE: Direct confirmation that bypassing CoWoS packaging gives Cerebras a structural lead times advantage over Nvidia and AMD.
Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein Research) — GAAP vs Core Revenue Divergence & Customer Warrant Amortization

Question: Bob, GAAP revenue missed consensus at $210.8M while Core revenue beat at $230.9M. Can you walk through the $20M delta and specifically how customer warrant amortization will impact reported GAAP margins over the next four quarters?

Executive Answer: Bob Komin (CFO): 'The $20.1M variance is entirely non-cash amortization associated with strategic customer equity warrants granted at the time of multi-gigawatt contracted capacity signings. As cloud inference volumes ramp and hardware deliveries accelerate in Q4, that non-cash discount diminishes as a percentage of top-line, which is why our Core gross margin expands directly to 47%-49% next quarter.'

Forensic Assessment: ACCOUNTING CLARITY: Demonstrates that the GAAP revenue optical 'miss' was purely non-cash warrant timing, while underlying cash collections and Core revenues surged.
Vivek Arya (BofA Securities) — CapEx Surge & Free Cash Flow Burn Runway

Question: You spent $497M on CapEx in Q3 and burned $871M in True Free Cash Flow. At what point does data center build-out peak, and when do customer cash deposits turn operating cash flow sustainably positive?

Executive Answer: Bob Komin (CFO): 'CapEx in Q2 and Q3 represented front-loaded capital deployment to secure 700 MW of high-density powered shell capacity across North America and Europe. We are sitting on $7.8 billion in cash and short-term liquid investments plus an undrawn $850 million credit facility. With Q4 operating margins reaching breakeven (-1% to +1%), operating cash flow inflects sharply in the first half of 2027 as customer deposits on our $25.4B backlog convert.'

Forensic Assessment: FORTRESS BALANCE SHEET: $7.8B liquid reserves eliminates dilutive financing risk despite near-term capital expenditure intensity.
